# 2 Kings Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 233r–233v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_012_page_001.jpg, 2KI_012_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.

**2** Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

**3** Nevertheless, the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

**4** Joash said to the priests, "All the silver of the sacred donations that is brought into the house of the LORD — the silver collected from each person assessed, and all the silver that anyone voluntarily brings into the house of the LORD —

**5** let the priests receive it, each from his donor, and let them repair the damages of the house, wherever any damage is found."

**6** But by the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damages of the house.

**7** Therefore King Joash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damages of the house? Now therefore do not accept any more silver from your donors, but hand it over for the repair of the house."

**8** The priests agreed that they would neither accept silver from the people nor repair the house themselves.

**9** Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid. He set it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the silver that was brought into the house of the LORD.

**10** Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of silver in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest came up, and they bagged and counted the silver that was found in the house of the LORD.

**11** They gave the weighed silver into the hands of the workers who had oversight of the house of the LORD. They in turn paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the house of the LORD,

**12** and to the masons and stonecutters, as well as for buying timber and quarried stone to repair the damages of the house of the LORD — for all that was spent on repairing the house.

**13** However, no silver basins, snuffers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any vessels of gold or silver were made from the silver brought into the house of the LORD,

**14** for it was given to the workers, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.

**15** They did not require an accounting from the men into whose hands they gave the silver to pay the workers, for they dealt faithfully.

**16** The silver from the guilt offerings and the silver from the sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.

**17** At that time Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it. Then Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

**18** Joash king of Judah took all the sacred things that Jehoshaphat, Joram, and Ahaziah his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own sacred gifts, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. So Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.

**19** Now the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

**20** His servants arose and formed a conspiracy, and struck down Joash at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.

**21** It was Jozachar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him down, and he died. They buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter is structured around a single irony: Joash restores the temple only to empty it. The detailed account of the temple repair system (vv.4–16) — priestly failure, royal intervention, Jehoiada's chest innovation, faithful workers — serves as the theological high point of Joash's reign. The abrupt shift to Hazael's threat and the stripping of temple treasures (vv.17–18) undoes everything. The assassination (vv.20–21) completes the downward trajectory. The narrator's qualification in v.2 — that Joash did right only while Jehoiada instructed him — is the interpretive key: this king's righteousness was dependent, not intrinsic. Hebrew verse numbering is followed throughout (12:1–22 Hebrew; many English versions number 11:21–12:21).

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "instructed him" vs. "guided him"
- **EMET:** "instructed-him [horahu]"
- **LOGOS:** "instructed him"
- **PNEUMA:** "guided him"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "instructed him" — the Hebrew *horahu* (from *yarah*, to teach/instruct) specifically means taught or directed; "guided" is too vague.

### V.5 — "acquaintance/donor" vs. "contacts"
- **EMET:** "his-acquaintance [makkaro]"
- **LOGOS:** "his donor"
- **PNEUMA:** "his own contacts"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his donor" — *makkar* implies a familiar/known person from whom silver is regularly received; "donor" communicates the financial relationship more clearly than "acquaintance."

### V.7 — "summoned" vs. "called in" vs. "demanded"
- **EMET:** "And-called"
- **LOGOS:** "summoned"
- **PNEUMA:** "called in... and demanded"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "summoned" — formal English befitting a royal address; PNEUMA's "demanded" adds a tone not explicitly in the Hebrew.

### V.9 — "bored a hole" vs. "came up with a solution"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** describe the physical action
- **PNEUMA:** adds interpretive framing ("came up with a solution")
- **SOPHIA ruling:** follows EMET/LOGOS — the text simply narrates the action; editorial framing belongs in notes, not translation.

### V.20 — "Beth-millo on the road going down to Silla" vs. "on the descent of Silla"
- **EMET:** "the-house of-Millo', the-descent of-Silla'"
- **LOGOS:** "at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla"
- **PNEUMA:** "at Beth-millo, on the road going down to Silla"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla" — the location is uncertain; a descriptive rendering preserves the geographical reference without over-interpreting.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
